case.pattern_description: This undocumented fraud pattern involves making 4 online purchases between $460 and $500 within 27 minutes on a single card (totaling $1,921.59) to keep each transaction just under a $500 authorisation threshold. It affects cardholders whose compromised cards are used across both familiar devices and anomalous transaction bands. The pattern was found by an agent scanning the card's transaction window in the graph for same-band bursts after an analyst requested a monitoring alert review.

case.summary: An analyst reviewed card C01890-K1 following a monitoring alert for structuring involving four online purchases totaling $1,921.59 made within 27 minutes. The transactions were kept just under a $500 authorization threshold, and the card had one confirmed fraud case in the preceding 45 days along with eight similar closed cases flagged as confirmed fraud. The verdict is fraud with an undocumented pattern, representing an exposure of $1,921.59. The system has automatically created a case and escalated the matter to an analyst, while blocking the card and filing a report await human approval.

sar.narrative: Customer C01890, holder of card C01890-K1, is the subject of this suspicious activity report following a monitoring alert for structuring. Between 2016-11-23 18:00 and 2016-11-23 18:27, four online transactions totaling $1,921.59 were executed on the card using device profile 'Moto E (4) Plus Build/NMA26.42-69 |  | chrome generic | '. These transactions included amounts of $469.82 (3481356, 2016-11-23 18:00), $467.06 (3481393, 2016-11-23 18:11), $496.08 (3481403, 2016-11-23 18:16), and $488.63 (3481444, 2016-11-23 18:27). The amounts were kept just under a $500 authorization threshold and occurred within 27 minutes, which raised suspicion of deliberate structuring. Additionally, the $496.08 transaction exceeded the card's 95th percentile of $158.22 against a median of $32.56. The suspicious device profile was previously used on this card for six prior transactions before the alert. The card had one confirmed fraud case in the 45 days prior to the alert under CC-4983, indicating the number may still be compromised, and eight of the eight most similar closed cases—including CC-3452, CC-5157, CC-5093, and CC-5414—were confirmed fraud. In response to this activity, the bank has executed automatic actions including creating a case and escalating to an analyst, while pending human approval for blocking the card and filing this report.
